name: MLB-M2 game-shape reality-gap branch
summary: Draft MLB parent cartridge branched from the current MLB-M0 behavior. M2 keeps the M0 app and publish contracts, then adds a game-shape/reality-gap layer that asks whether the side, total, first-five, and first-inning reads match the way the game is likely to unfold.
keyImprovements: Branches a full parent cartridge from MLB-M0 without activating it, so M2 can be benchmarked against M0 before public use.
Adds `analysis.gameShape`, a structured read of phase agreement, crooked-inning chaos, dead-early shape, bullpen-flip risk, and projection-vs-reality gap.
Adds an RF research lens that treats RandomForest results as a nonlinear reality check, with totals as the only currently deployable RF lane from the research docs.
Keeps ML/F5 RF influence downgraded until bucketed backtests show it beats the current M0 logic.
Names market implications separately for side, first-five, total, and first inning so M2 can stop forcing moneyline when the game shape says another lane is cleaner.

keyMetrics.label: Branch source
keyMetrics.details: M2 was scaffolded from the current M0 cartridge and is registered as a draft.

keyMetrics.label: Active model
keyMetrics.details: M2 is not active. The registry still points daily/public runs at M0 until M2 passes comparison checks.

keyMetrics.label: RF lane trust
keyMetrics.details: Historical RF research marked totals deployable; moneyline, first-five, and first-inning stay advisory only.

keyMetrics.label: New output
keyMetrics.details: M2 emits reality-gap score, chaos score, dead-early score, phase split score, RF impact score, and lane-specific market implications.

notes: M2 is not a promise that RF is better. It is the branch where RF impact can finally be measured instead of hand-waved.
The core question is whether the model can describe game flow before choosing a bet: early scoring, first-five control, bridge innings, total chaos, and conversion failure.
A high reality-gap score should downgrade blind full-game ML confidence even when the raw side model has a strong lean.
Future M2 work should persist per-game reality-gap outcomes so we can backtest whether high-gap labels predicted bad ML bets, better F5 bets, better totals, or passes.
knownLimitations: The RF lens currently uses documented research baselines, not a newly serialized production RF artifact.
M2 has not been activated and should not publish public picks until M0-vs-M2 comparison artifacts exist.
The first game-shape formula is intentionally transparent and testable; it still needs day-by-day settlement to prove lift.
